answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each identity expensive to mint and cheap to verify: require every agent to post a locked bond and complete a peer-checked proof-of-work task before it can trade. Like a quartz vein that yields only one gem per claim, or an onyx seal stamped by a single island registry, duplicates become visible — the same bond, task, or registry entry cannot back two agents. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must pay a thousand bonds plus a thousand units of compute and waiting time, while honest agents pay once, so flooding costs more than it earns.
